subject: Any function in package secr that estimates the average direction of subsequent spatial recaptures?

messages.author: bdbdd16043b71751
messages.subject: Any function in package secr that estimates the average direction of subsequent spatial recaptures?
parts: I'm interested if my organisms are moving in certain directions across the landscape. Is there a function in package secr that estimates the average direction of subsequent spatial recaptures?

messages.author: 2c49652a5796ed9c
messages.subject: Re: Any function in package secr that estimates the average direction of subsequent spatial recaptures?
parts: It might help if we had a better understanding of the process of directional movement you have in mind.  Do you think activity centers move directionally across occasions?  If so, you could perhaps modify the markov movement model of Royle et al. (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10144-015-0524-z) to have directional movement.  If you think animal movement is elongated along a major axis and reduced along a minor axis around fixed activity centers, you could perhaps try the anisotropic detection functions I used in this paper (http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jwmg.21144/full) to infer bears preferentially moved along linear ridges.  It has code to implement in secr.  In the first model, the order of the detections would matter while in the second model, the order does not.  Or maybe you have something else in mind.

messages.subject: Re: Any function in package secr that estimates the average direction of subsequent spatial recaptures?
parts:
In addition to Ben's suggestion, it's possible to characterise space use asymmetry as a function of a landscape covariate (e.g. elevation). This can be done easily in secr following the non-euclidean vignette.

Chris
